**Work Location:** On site

ZenRiva Capital Holdings is seeking a Senior Financial Analyst to provide the analysis, reporting, and financial insight that support sound investment and business decisions.

This is not a purely reporting-focused role. You will be expected to understand the story behind the numbers, challenge assumptions, and give senior stakeholders a clear view of performance, risk, and opportunity.

You will work closely with finance leadership and operational stakeholders on planning, forecasting, investment analysis, and portfolio reporting. The role requires strong technical ability, but also the judgement to know what matters most in a decision.

Your work will include:

* Build and maintain financial models for forecasting, budgeting, investment evaluation, and scenario planning.

* Support monthly and quarterly management reporting, including income statements, cash flow, balance-sheet analysis, and variance commentary.
* Prepare financial materials for leadership reviews, investment discussions, and strategic planning.
* Review business cases, capital requests, and investment opportunities, including return analysis and sensitivity testing.
* Partner with operational teams to improve the quality of financial inputs, assumptions, and performance reporting.

* Assist with annual budgeting and rolling forecast cycles.
* Support due diligence, data-room preparation, and financial analysis connected with new initiatives or portfolio activity.

What you will bring

* Five or more years of experience in financial analysis, FP&A, corporate finance, investment analysis, transaction advisory, or a related field.
* Advanced Excel skills and the ability to build clear, reliable financial models from the ground up.
* Strong understanding of financial statements, cash flow, budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis.
* Experience presenting financial findings to senior leaders or non-finance stakeholders.

**About Clipboard**
===================

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. ===================

As a Documents Compliance Analyst, you own the compliance decisions behind whether a healthcare professional is cleared to work: background check disqualifications, credential and risk review, and how new state requirements get implemented. You set the standard the team applies, and you are the named decision-maker when a case is hard. What the law requires is a given. How we meet it is up to you, and you own that call.

This is not a people management role. The work is recurring by design. The same categories of questions arrive every week, alongside state license renewals and reporting that run on a fixed calendar and never finish. Your value is in reaching the same well-reasoned decision every time and documenting your reasoning well enough that others can apply it. * Serve as the named escalation point for background check disqualification decisions
* Make the initial call on agency compliance implementation
* Handle escalations on worker credential verification, including license violations and reprimands
* Decide which questions you resolve and document yourself, and which warrant partnering with Legal

**Written analysis**

* Produce risk analyses in a consistent format: the question, your research, your reasoning, your recommended path.
* Evaluate new state and agency requirements before implementation, quantifying what compliance costs a worker in time, money, and completion rate, and recommending how we implement.
* Build and maintain the decision record that lets other people reach the same conclusion you would

**Recurring compliance operations**

* Own the credential verification audits
* Plan and drive the implementation of high-value requirements, such as continuing education

* Ongoing state reporting

  + background screening adjudicator

* Experience interpreting statutes, regulations, or agency guidance and turning them into operational requirements.

* You can reach a defensible decision when documentation is incomplete or unavailable, and you're explicit about what your reasoning rests on.
* You can read complex regulatory material and work out how it applies in practice to a marketplace model.
* You weigh compliance risk against business impact and find the path that meets the requirement without restricting more than it demands.
* You write decision memos and business cases that leadership can act on.
* You build credibility with people who don't report to you.
* You own recurring work with hard deadlines, such as license renewals and state reporting.

This is a hands-on buying role—not just an administrative position. You'll represent the business at card shows, develop relationships with collectors and dealers, negotiate purchases within established guidelines, and ensure every deal is accurately documented, paid, and reflected in our inventory systems.

The ideal candidate is comfortable making deals face-to-face and equally committed to keeping accurate records behind the scenes.

**What you'll do:**
===================

### **Buying & Relationship Development**

* Travel to card shows and buying events to source inventory and establish new relationships.
* Build and maintain a network of collectors, dealers, and other inventory sources.
* Develop repeat buying opportunities through consistent outreach, follow-up, and reliable deal execution.

### **Deal Execution & Payments**

* Document each purchase, including the seller, cards acquired, agreed pricing, payment terms, and delivery arrangements.
* Coordinate timely payments to sellers and customers for completed, approved deals using Ramp and other approved payment methods.
* Verify payment information and supporting documentation before submitting or releasing payments.
* Track open invoices, outstanding payments, and unresolved deal items through completion.
* Communicate clearly with sellers about payment status, shipping, and any discrepancies.

### **Inventory & Financial Accountability**

* Own the workflow from purchase through inventory intake, ensuring every acquired item has an accurate digital record.
* Maintain inventory details such as player, year, set, card number, variation, grade, certification number where applicable, purchase cost, and storage location.
* Record item-level costs for individual cards and allocate costs across bulk purchases using an agreed methodology.
* Match inventory records to purchase documentation and payment confirmations so every item can be traced back to its acquisition.
* Track inventory in transit, received, stored, sold, returned, or consigned, as applicable.
* Reconcile physical inventory with digital records and investigate missing items, duplicate entries, or incorrect costs.
* Provide organized records to support bookkeeping and ensure purchase totals, payments, and recorded inventory costs agree.

### **Workflow Ownership**

* Keep buying trackers, inventory spreadsheets, and payment records accurate and current.
* Establish repeatable processes for show purchases, seller follow-up, inventory intake, and reconciliation.
* Maintain a clear view of pending shipments, unpaid deals, unlogged inventory, and other outstanding tasks.
* Coordinate with bookkeeping, sales, and fulfillment partners to ensure clean handoffs.
* Identify process improvements that reduce manual work, prevent errors, and help the business scale.

* Strong knowledge of all trading cards (sports and gaming), including pricing, grading, condition, and market trends.
* Experience buying, selling, or negotiating sports card deals.
* Ability to build trust and maintain productive relationships with collectors and dealers.
* Willingness and ability to travel regularly, including weekends for card shows.

**Preferred:** An established buying network, experience sourcing at card shows, and familiarity with Ramp or similar payment platforms.

* A growing network of reliable sellers and repeat buying opportunities.
* Purchases that align with buying criteria, budgets, and margin targets.
